mcqs.learning_point: Recognise squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombi and trapezia
mcqs.question: Consider a quadrilateral that satisfies all three statements: (i) Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. (ii) All four sides are equal. (iii) All interior angles are right angles. Which quadrilateral meets all these conditions?
mcqs.explanation: A square has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, all sides equal, and each interior angle 90°. A rectangle has right angles but adjacent sides can differ. A rhombus has equal sides but angles are not necessarily right. A parallelogram lacks the right-angle requirement. Hence the correct answer is Square.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand relationships among different quadrilateral classes
mcqs.question: In the hierarchy of quadrilaterals, which of the following statements is true?
mcqs.explanation: A square satisfies all the properties of a rectangle (opposite sides parallel and all angles right), so every square is a rectangle. Not every rectangle has equal sides, so A is false. A trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides, not necessarily both, so C is false. A rhombus has equal sides but its angles need not be right, so D is false.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a quadrilateral?
mcqs.explanation: A quadrilateral is a polygon that has exactly four straight sides, four vertices, and four interior angles. The other options describe triangles, pentagons, and hexagons respectively.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify sides, vertices and angles of quadrilaterals
mcqs.question: How many sides, vertices, and interior angles does a quadrilateral have?
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a quadrilateral has four sides, each meeting at a vertex, giving four vertices, and consequently four interior angles. The other options miscount one or more elements.

mcqs.question: Which quadrilateral is defined as having opposite sides equal in length, with exactly two distinct side lengths each occurring twice?
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle has opposite sides equal (two distinct lengths) and each length appears twice. A square has all sides equal, a rhombus also has all sides equal, and a trapezium does not require opposite sides to be equal.

mcqs.question: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel and exactly two right angles?
mcqs.explanation: A right-angled trapezium (right trapezoid) has one pair of parallel sides and two adjacent right angles. Squares and rectangles have two pairs of parallel sides and four right angles. A rhombus has no right angles unless it is a square.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombi and trapezia
mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has four equal sides, opposite sides are parallel, and each interior angle measures 90°. Which quadrilateral is it?
mcqs.explanation: All four sides equal and all angles 90° uniquely describe a square. A rectangle has right angles but adjacent sides can differ. A parallelogram may have equal opposite sides but not necessarily right angles. A trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand relationships among different quadrilateral classes
mcqs.question: A student draws a quadrilateral that is both a rectangle and a rhombus. What specific quadrilateral has been drawn?
mcqs.explanation: The only quadrilateral that satisfies the definitions of both a rectangle (all angles 90°) and a rhombus (all sides equal) is a square. Hence the shape is a square. The other options do not meet both criteria.
